title: A down-set counterexample to Smyth's injection conjecture on compositions (Conjecture 1.5 of arXiv:1512.04084; Order 35 (2018))
exact_endpoint: Smyth1512.not_conjecture15 : ¬ Smyth1512.Conjecture15, where Conjecture15 := ∀ A a B b : ℕ, B ≤ A → b ≤ a → ∃ γ : (U A b × U B a) → (U A a × U B b), Function.Injective γ ∧ ∀ x, Dom (concat x.1.1 x.2.1) (concat (γ x).1.1 (γ x).2.1); U m n = compositions Fin m → ℕ of sum n; Dom = dominance (equal sums, all prefix sums) of non-increasing rearrangements; concat = Fin.append
scope: Smyth's Conjecture 1.5: for all A ≥ B ≥ 0 and a ≥ b ≥ 0 there is a dominance-decreasing injection U^A_b × U^B_a → U^A_a × U^B_b. False at (A, a, B, b) = (3, 20, 2, 19): the down-set of 8 explicit partitions of 39 contains the rearranged concatenations of 1137 domain elements but only 1134 target elements.

substantive_reason: It refutes a published combinatorial conjecture proposed as a route to total-nonnegativity inequalities, by an exact finite certificate found only well beyond the obvious ranges (every case with A, B, a, b ≤ 10 and a + b ≤ 16 passes; the first failure in the scanned shapes is at a + b = 39). The proof is a short pigeonhole argument on an explicit down-set. Significance is modest: the conjecture is low-profile and not needed for the source's theorems.
